before: For normal author declarations, later layers outrank earlier layers. For important author declarations, that layer order reverses: an earlier layer outranks a later one. This comparison stays within the same origin and excludes active transitions.

!important is a declaration flag after the value and before the semicolon, not part of the color. @layer base, theme establishes the order before the rules. Both declarations here are important, so base wins even though theme appears later. Removing both flags restores normal layer order and theme wins. User and browser important origins have their own precedence; do not describe this as a universal strongest-rule trick.

Keep the two named layers and make the earlier important base declaration protect the teal text. Supplied checks inspect the authored contract and may temporarily change a value to compare the stated behavior; temporary values are restored. You are writing CSS, not these JavaScript test helpers.
after: For normal rules in these stylesheets, the later layer wins. When both values use `!important`, the earlier layer wins instead. This comparison is between rules from the same page, with no active transition.
`!important` is a flag written after the value and before the semicolon. It changes the rule's priority; it is not part of the color name.

Removing both important flags makes these normal rules again. The later theme layer then wins with purple. Important rules from the user or browser have other priorities, so this is not a rule that always beats everything.

before.question: After removing !important from both declarations, which color wins?
choices: Purple from the later theme layer.
before.explanation: Layer priority reverses specifically for important declarations; normal declarations use the ordinary later-layer priority.

after.question: Which color wins after !important is removed from both rules?
choices: Teal, because earlier layers always win
Neither, because layers need important flags
Purple, from the later theme layer
after.explanation: Without the flags, normal layer order applies. The later theme layer wins.
